output.answer: Synchrony Bank's class action history centers on debt-collection calls, securities fraud, and CareCredit lending. Most recently, on June 17, 2026, Iman Habel filed a pending putative nationwide class action (Habel v. Synchrony Bank, No. 3:26-cv-03349-AJB-BJW, S.D. Cal.) alleging the bank made more than 100 prerecorded debt-collection calls after she revoked consent and retained counsel, in violation of the TCPA and California's Rosenthal Act. Earlier, Lucas v. Synchrony Bank (N.D. Ind.) ended in a $2.6 million TCPA settlement — finally approved April 25, 2023, with payments to class members beginning in early 2024 — over prerecorded calls about Synchrony accounts that did not belong to the recipients. In re Synchrony Financial Securities Litigation (D. Conn., No. 3:18-cv-1818) settled for $34 million (final approval August 2023; distributions running through August 2026) over statements tied to the 2018 GE/Walmart portfolio transition, and a pending putative class action filed August 19, 2024 in the E.D.N.Y. (S.G. v. Synchrony Bank) alleges CareCredit deferred-interest lending violates New York usury law, though the court has recommended compelling arbitration. Related but not class actions: a $3.5 million 2021 civil judgment by California district attorneys over collection calls and a 2014 CFPB/DOJ enforcement matter totaling roughly $225 million.
caveats: Habel v. Synchrony Bank and S.G. v. Synchrony Bank are pending, putative class actions — the allegations are unproven and no court has ruled on the merits; Habel also awaits class certification.

The Lucas v. Synchrony Bank settlement is closed; individual payouts were estimated at $35-$140 and readers of Top Class Actions reported receiving about $40.11 in early 2024, so that figure is anecdotal.
The $34 million Synchrony Financial securities settlement was brought on behalf of stock purchasers of the parent, Synchrony Financial — not bank customers.

The 2021 $3.5 million California district attorneys' judgment and the 2014 CFPB/DOJ ~$225 million consumer-relief order were government enforcement actions, not class actions, and are background only.
A September 2026 FCRA credit-reporting suit (Saavedra v. Synchrony Bank, C.D. Cal., No. 2:26-cv-06230) was reported as an individual action, not a class action, and is excluded from the list above.
This list covers the prominently reported class actions; it is not a comprehensive PACER docket of every suit naming Synchrony Bank.

output.question: What class action lawsuits has Synchrony Bank faced?

key_facts.fact: Habel v. Synchrony Bank, Case No. 3:26-cv-03349-AJB-BJW, a putative nationwide class action under the TCPA and California Rosenthal Act, was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of California on June 17, 2026, alleging Synchrony used prerecorded-voice calls to collect a debt after the plaintiff revoked consent.

The Habel complaint alleges the plaintiff revoked consent and retained counsel on Jan. 12, 2026, after which Synchrony allegedly continued calling her cellphone with prerecorded voice messages more than 100 times.

In Lucas v. Synchrony Bank (No. 4:21-cv-00070-PPS-JEM, N.D. Ind.), the court granted final approval on April 25, 2023 to a $2,600,000 settlement fund over TCPA claims for prerecorded calls about Synchrony accounts that did not belong to the call recipients (class period Oct. 16, 2020-Nov. 18, 2022).
Settlement payments from the Lucas v. Synchrony Bank $2.6 million TCPA settlement began in early 2024, with readers reporting payouts of about $40.11; estimated individual payments were $35-$140.

In re Synchrony Financial Securities Litigation (No. 3:18-cv-1818-VAB, D. Conn.), a securities class action on behalf of purchasers of Synchrony Financial common stock from Jan. 19, 2018 through July 12, 2018, settled for $34,000,000 in cash; final judgment was entered Aug. 7, 2023 and distributions occurred in 2024, 2025 and 2026.

S.G. v. Synchrony Bank, a putative class action filed Aug. 19, 2024 in the E.D.N.Y. (No. 2:24-cv-05788), alleges CareCredit loans violate New York usury laws and consumer-protection statutes on behalf of CareCredit account holders who accrued interest above 16% per annum; a magistrate judge recommended granting Synchrony's motion to compel arbitration.

In 2021, a multijurisdictional team of California district attorneys secured a $3.5 million civil judgment against Synchrony Bank over allegedly unreasonably frequent and harassing collection calls; the judgment was entered without an admission of wrongdoing (an enforcement action, not a class action).

In June 2014 the CFPB and DOJ brought a joint enforcement action against Synchrony's predecessor, GE Capital Retail Bank, over deceptive credit-card marketing and discriminatory exclusion of Hispanic borrowers from debt-relief offers, requiring roughly $225 million in consumer relief plus a $3.5 million civil penalty; the consent order was terminated May 12, 2025 (enforcement, not a class action).
